System blueprint

A clear client and partner portal

Give customers or partners an authenticated view of the information and actions they need. Connect status, requests, deliverables, approvals, and selected notifications around a clear shared service journey.

Level 2Choose a capability

Customers can lose clarity when project updates and documents arrive across separate channels. A useful portal needs a defined purpose, organization-level record boundaries, clear permissions, and an operating owner for the service behind the interface.

Useful outputs

  • A portal scope, user journeys, and approved role and organization access model.
  • A responsive portal for selected records, requests, deliverables, and actions.
  • Tested handoffs and notification workflows with visible exceptions.
  • Customer onboarding, administrator guidance, and deployment and support handover.

Inputs we need

  • A defined shared journey, customer and partner roles, and record ownership.
  • Approved source records, organization identifiers, documents, and access boundaries.
  • Notification and approval rules, provider access, and support and release ownership.
Level 3Explore a focus

Define the shared journey

Map the agreed customer or partner roles, shared records, requests, approvals, and notifications. Confirm which systems own each record and the information boundary for each organization.

  • Apply approved state transitions and record the responsible action or approval.
  • Route failed notifications, invalid requests, and missing records for investigation.
  • Approve the information boundary and each role before importing or exposing records.
  • Validate client-facing content, notifications, and approval expectations.
  • Review test evidence for organization separation, account recovery, and mobile use.

Build the portal and handoffs

Implement the selected interface, access model, and data paths. Add only the required approval, notification, or payment workflows and validate provider and plan feasibility.

Human expertise

Own the judgment.

Service owners decide what is shared and who can act. Designers and engineers validate usability, organization boundaries, access, release behaviour, and the support process.

AI assistance

Support the process.

AI may assist preparation, search, or drafting within approved information boundaries. It should not change access, approve client deliverables, or make unsupported customer commitments.
